annotation.value: Returns an array of strings; each element is one JSON-serialized layout object (manual layouts enriched with origin/visibility/allow-lists, plus autotile algorithm entries). A template entry carries isScrollingTemplate true, and its id is a plain braced UUID with no scheme prefix, so that flag is the only thing distinguishing it from a manual layout entry (autotile entries stay recognisable by their 'autotile:' prefix).

A template entry's id is a plain braced UUID with no scheme prefix — the isScrollingTemplate flag is the discriminator, as in getLayoutList. annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Create or update a scrolling template from its JSON object. An empty or missing id creates a fresh template. Editing a bundled template writes a user copy that shadows it. Names longer than 40 characters and descriptions longer than 500 characters are shortened to fit. A save whose stored result is identical to the existing entry rewrites nothing and does not emit scrollingTemplatesChanged. Returns the stored template UUID, or empty when the template is invalid.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Delete the user file of the scrolling template with the given id. Deleting a user copy that shadowed a bundled template resurfaces the bundled original, and a pure bundled template is refused. The id is scrubbed from every assignment rule and from every quick layout slot only when it no longer resolves to any template after the delete, so a resurfaced bundled original keeps its live assignments. The scrub reaches assignment rules and quick slots only. A context in SCROLLING mode is not merely scrubbed: its template slot is rewritten to the literal "none", so the screen ends up with no template rather than inheriting the configured default. That is what deleting the template a screen was actually using means, and an empty slot would have handed the screen to whatever other template happened to be the default. A context in another mode, where the slot is only a remembered value, keeps the plain clear. A deleted id still named by the Scrolling default-template SETTING is a different case and is deliberately left in place: it resolves to no template at read time and those contexts fall back to the engine's compiled defaults, so nothing has to rewrite the user's setting behind their back.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Returns all screen-to-layout assignments as JSON. This is a READBACK of *stored* assignment state, not a payload the batch setter accepts: setAllScreenAssignments takes a flat screenId-to-layoutId string map, while this answers a JSON string of connector-keyed per-screen objects, so the pair does not round-trip. Synthesized level-1 global-default fallbacks are deliberately NOT serialized, so callers that need the resolved mode for an unconfigured screen must use the per-context lookup methods instead. Only screens with at least one stored entry (base or per-desktop) appear; for screen enumeration use getAvailableScreenIds.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: JSON object keyed by connector name, containing one entry per screen with stored assignments. Each entry includes {"screenId": <stable-id>}. Screens with an explicit base-level assignment additionally include "mode" plus whichever of {"default", "snappingLayout", "tilingAlgorithm", "scrollingTemplate"} the entry actually stores (an empty field is omitted, so a missing key means unset, not empty-string; "scrollingTemplate" carries the literal "none" for a context that explicitly uses no template, which is a stored value and so is NOT omitted); screens with explicit per-desktop assignments include numeric-string keys ("1", "2", …) mapping to the assigned layout id. Screens with no stored entries are omitted entirely — DO NOT use this method to enumerate available screens; call getAvailableScreenIds instead. Per-desktop keys are enumerated up to the compositor's CURRENT desktop count, so a stored entry for a desktop above that count (the user reduced their desktop count) is not serialized and the round trip is lossy for it. When the desktop count is unavailable the count falls back to 1, so desktop 1 is still serialized and only desktops 2 and up are dropped.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString

Unlike getAllScreenAssignments this is the resolved value (including synthesized global-default fallbacks), which is what the ActiveLayout rule field matches against. Pair with activeLayoutForScreenChanged: fetch once on daemon-ready, then track the signal.

annotation.value: Batch set all per-activity assignments (saves once). Key format: 'screenId|activityId' (legacy ':' fallback accepted). Clears existing assignments of this family first: a key absent from the map is DELETED, so a partial map silently drops every assignment it omits.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Map of 'screenId|activityId' keys to a plain layoutId string (a Scrolling context stays the bare 'scrolling:' sentinel). Only that string is read here. The matching getter's value is a wider {layoutId, scrollingTemplate} map, and the scrolling template is written through setScrollingTemplateLayout, never through the batch setters.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Map of 'screenId|activityId' keys to a map {layoutId, scrollingTemplate}: layoutId is the assignment id the matching batch setter accepts (a Scrolling context stays the bare 'scrolling:' sentinel), scrollingTemplate the context's scrolling-template UUID, or empty when the context pins none of its own, or the literal "none" when it explicitly uses no template at all. The getter value is deliberately wider than the setter's plain layoutId string; the template is written through setScrollingTemplateLayout, never through the batch setters.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Batch set all per-(screen,desktop,activity) Combined assignments (saves once). Key format: 'screenId|virtualDesktop|activityId'. Pure-Activity, pure-Desktop and Monitor-only rules are not touched. Clears existing assignments of this family first: a key absent from the map is DELETED, so a partial map silently drops every assignment it omits.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Get layout for screen, virtual desktop, and activity. Falls through to the global default layout when that context has no assignment, INCLUDING when the default is suppressed for it, so it can report a layout where getActiveLayoutsForScreens omits the screen and getScreenStates reports none. Callers wanting the suppression-aware resolved value must use one of those instead.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Assign a native scrolling template to the context and flip it to Scrolling mode. The value is a ScrollingTemplate UUID (one of the ids getScrollingTemplates reports), whose column blueprint seeds new columns and whose preset lists become the strip's vocabulary. Besides a UUID the field takes two reserved forms: the empty string, which clears the context's own choice so it inherits the configured default template, and the literal "none", which means the context explicitly uses NO template and is honoured over that default. Any other id the template store does not know, and any other non-UUID string, is rejected and nothing is written, so the context keeps its previous template. The existence half of that check needs the template store wired: an embedder running the daemon libraries without one (unit fixtures) gets the UUID-format check only, and a well-formed but unknown id is stored, then degrades to no template when the strip reads it. The mode flip applies to the empty-id clear form too, which is the one case where it is not implied by the argument: clearing the template still forces the context to Scrolling and materializes a stored entry for it if none existed. To remove the context's assignment outright, call clearAssignmentForScreenDesktopActivity, or clearAssignmentForScreenDesktop when the context names no activity — this setter accepts an empty activityId and the Combined clear does not, so the three-dimension clear refuses exactly the Desktop-family contexts this setter can create.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Scrolling template UUID to assign (from getScrollingTemplates), or empty to clear the context's own choice so it inherits the configured default, or the literal "none" to use no template at all regardless of that default. All three forms force the context to Scrolling mode.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Resolved scrolling template for the context. A context that names no template of its own falls back to the configured default template, so the answer is empty only when the context is not Scrolling, or when neither the context nor the configured default names a template the store still holds. This is the RESOLVED answer, not the stored field, so it cannot distinguish a context that pins nothing from one set explicitly to "none" — both resolve to no template and both read back empty. Use getScreenStates, whose scrollingTemplateId carries the stored value verbatim, to tell those two apart.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Set a complete assignment entry (mode + snapping layout + tiling algorithm) for a screen/desktop/activity context. Settings app sends one full entry per staged context during save. The entry is seeded from the context's stored one first, so a scrolling template already assigned there survives the call even though this signature does not carry it; setScrollingTemplateLayout remains the only way to change it.

annotation.value: Screen ID.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Virtual desktop index (1-based, 0 = screen-level).

annotation.value: KDE Activity ID (empty = all activities).

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Mode (0=Snapping, 1=Autotile, 2=Scrolling). Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Snapping layout UUID (empty = unset).

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Suppress screenLayoutChanged signals while the settings app replays a batch of assignment mutations during save. Always paired: setSaveBatchMode(true) before the batch, setSaveBatchMode(false) after. applyAssignmentChanges also releases the suppression itself, before its empty-batch check, so a client that dies mid-batch cannot mute the signal for the rest of the daemon's life.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: True to enter batch mode, false to leave it.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Trigger resnap/retile + OSD after a batch of assignment changes. Settings app calls this once after all setAssignmentEntry/clear calls complete. Releases the setSaveBatchMode suppression first, then returns without applying anything when the batch staged no screens, so a call with no preceding mutation is a no-op rather than a resnap of every window.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when the daemon has fully initialized and is ready. Clients (KCM, KWin effect) should wait for this before querying layouts.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when the internal active layout changes. Carries the transient active-layout UUID, which may differ from getActiveLayout()'s settings-based default.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: UUID of the newly active layout.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Refresh hint for subscribers holding quick layout slot state, such as the settings panel's slot cards. Emitted when the slots are modified directly, unconditionally when a layout is deleted, and when a scrolling template's deletion scrub changed a rule or swept a slot. Re-read the slots rather than assuming a specific slot changed.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted after applyAssignmentChanges finishes a KCM save batch, listing the screens whose assignments changed. Skipped entirely for an empty batch. Also emitted by the daemon's own rule reconcile when a rule edit moves a screen's resolved assignment, so it is not exclusive to KCM saves.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Screen IDs whose assignments were modified in the batch.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when the current KDE Activity changes.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: New current activity ID.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when the list of activities changes.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when the number of virtual desktops changes.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: New virtual desktop count.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted on structural layout mutations (updateLayout, the editor's save path) and on every active-layout switch, alongside the cheaper activeLayoutChanged(id). Usually carries the full layout JSON payload; when the update targeted an AUTOTILE entry the payload is instead the caller's raw autotile-override object (id 'autotile:<algorithmId>', not a serialized layout), so subscribers must not blindly parse it as a layout. createLayoutFromJson does not emit this; a new layout announces itself with layoutCreated(id). Scalar property mutations (hidden, autoAssign, aspectRatioClass) emit layoutPropertyChanged instead to avoid the full serialization.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Full layout as JSON.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Cheap context-switch notification: emitted alongside layoutChanged(json) on every active-layout switch, but carries only the layout UUID instead of the full JSON payload. Subscribers that re-load from disk (e.g. the editor) can bind to this signal and ignore the heavier layoutChanged emit.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: UUID of the newly active layout.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Compact per-property change notification. Replaces layoutChanged(json) for setLayoutHidden, setLayoutAutoAssign, and setLayoutAspectRatioClass. Subscribers that want the full shape should pull it via getLayout(layoutId) — the adaptor's cache is invalidated before the signal fires.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Layout UUID whose property changed.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Property name: 'hidden', 'autoAssign', or 'aspectRatioClass'.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: New value as a variant (bool or int).

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when the list of layouts changes.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when the scrolling-template store's loaded set changes (save, delete, duplicate, rescan).

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when a new layout is created (createLayout, createLayoutFromJson, duplicateLayout, importLayout). Carries the new layout's UUID.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: UUID of the newly created layout.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when a layout is deleted. Carries the UUID of the deleted layout.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: UUID of the deleted layout.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when a screen's layout assignment changes.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString

annotation.value: Assigned layout UUID.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Virtual desktop number (0 = display default).

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Emitted when a screen's RESOLVED active layout changes. The triggers are an assignment edit, a virtual-desktop or activity switch, a screen being added or removed, a virtual-screen reconfigure, a settings save that moves the global default, a rule edit that moves the assignment cascade, and a layout being deleted out from under a screen. This is the companion signal to getActiveLayoutsForScreens and the one to track for the ActiveLayout rule field. Unlike screenLayoutChanged, which reports assignment MUTATIONS and is suppressed during a KCM save batch, this reports every change to the value a rule would see.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Stable screen id whose active layout changed.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: The screen's new active layout id (a layout UUID in braces, or 'autotile:<algo>'). Empty when the screen no longer resolves to any layout.
